purpose: doc 57 / exp71 feasibility spike: can neutral-atom ANALOG control express the programme's intro-state family, and what does the realistic device model allow
boundedness: four questions, no verb block compiled, no exp71 file written, no committed artefact modified
Q3_finding: AnalogDevice -- Pulser's model of the realistic analog QPU -- exposes rydberg_global ONLY: no local addressing channel, NO detuning-map modulator, no SLM mask. DigitalAnalogDevice and MockDevice do carry local channels and DMMs, but neither is the analog QPU. Any exp71 design that needs per-atom differentiated control on the analog machine must therefore break the permutation symmetry with GEOMETRY, or move to a device class the programme has not been offered.

Q1_minimal_sequence.convention_determined_empirically: H = sum_i (Omega/2)(cos(phase) X_i + sin(phase) Y_i) - delta n_i + sum_{i<j} (C6/r_ij^6) n_i n_j, with |0> = ground and |1> = Rydberg; Pulser's emulator returns the state in the REVERSED per-atom basis. All four sign/ordering variants were tried and exactly one matched, so the convention is measured rather than quoted
Q1_minimal_sequence.note: the in-house expm model is used for the search below ONLY because it agrees with Pulser's emulator to the figure above; every reported reachability number is therefore a Pulser-consistent number, and the emulator re-verifies the best solutions at the end

Q2a_symmetry_control.statement: two identical atoms, one GLOBAL drive, a geometry invariant under their exchange: [H(t), SWAP] = 0 for every t and the initial state |00> is SWAP-even, so the evolved state is SWAP-even at all times and the two atoms' reduced states are IDENTICAL. Distinct per-referent angles are unreachable, and this is a theorem, not an optimisation failure.

r1_analog_global_only_2atom_symmetric.note: this is the SYMMETRIC CEILING: the best a global drive can do when the target asks for two different angles and the dynamics cannot tell the two atoms apart. It is not zero, because a symmetric state still overlaps an asymmetric target, and reading it as partial success would be the error the (a) theorem exists to prevent

r2_analog_global_only_asymmetric_geometr.symmetry_broken_by: geometry -- a third, undriven-by-design spectator atom placed so the two data atoms sit in DIFFERENT interaction environments; the atom positions are searched, subject to the device's own min separation (5.0 um) and max radius (38 um)
r2_analog_global_only_asymmetric_geometr.note: the spectator is TRACED OUT, so the reported number is the mixed-state fidelity of the two-wire register -- an UPPER bound on what a pure two-wire preparation could deliver, and the residual entanglement with the spectator is a cost the doc must account for

r3_local_detuning_idealised.device: NOT AnalogDevice -- AnalogDevice carries NO DMM (Q3). This is an IDEALISED local-detuning capability: sign-unconstrained, weight-unconstrained, constant over the sequence. The number is therefore an UPPER bound on any real DMM, whose detuning is negative-only, weight-limited to [0,1] and bottom-capped

r4_local_addressing_channel.reason: a rydberg_local channel addresses one atom at a time, so RY(theta_A) (x) RY(theta_B) is two targeted pulses and the preparation is exact up to pulse calibration
r4_local_addressing_channel.caveat: this is the DIGITAL-analog / mock class, not the analog QPU the collaboration would target; recording it keeps the distinction visible rather than letting a MockDevice success stand in for an AnalogDevice capability

Q2_verdict.reading: Two findings, and they point opposite ways. (1) Distinct per-referent angles are UNREACHABLE by symmetry under a global drive in a symmetric register -- proved, then confirmed to 5.8e-16. (2) Breaking that symmetry with GEOMETRY works, and works well: with a third atom placed asymmetrically and the positions searched under the device's own min-separation and max-radius limits, three real noun pairs reach F >= 0.9998 in the continuous-time propagator, inside the 6 us budget. So the intro-state family IS expressible on the analog device, and the route is geometric rather than pulse-clever. THE CATCH IS IN Q5: those solutions lose up to 0.14 fidelity when their pulse train is placed on the device's 4 ns clock. The expressibility question is answered YES; the ROBUSTNESS question is answered 'not by this search', and that is exp71's to fix by optimising on the device timebase.
Q2_verdict.honest_caveat: a search failure is never a proof of unreachability. Only the symmetric case (Q2a) is proved; every other number here is a LOWER bound on what better waveforms could reach.

Q4_duration_budget.item_needs_n_blocks_at_T1: intro + 1 verb block + 1 inverse block + 1 question effect = 4 compiled segments
Q4_duration_budget.arithmetic: 4 segments at exp37's UNCONSTRAINED median already exceeds the 6.0 us budget; exp37's solutions were found with the interaction strength V free and with no amplitude ceiling, so exp71's targets must be RE-SOLVED under Omega <= 12.566 rad/us, |delta| <= 125.664 rad/us and a total <= 6000 ns, at ONE fixed geometry. The budget is a live design constraint, not a formality.
Q4_duration_budget.caveat: exp37's taus are in the same rad/us convention but were solved against a FREE V; they are an order-of-magnitude reference, not a prediction of the constrained solution's duration
Q4_duration_budget.consequence: the INTRO ALONE, solved to F ~ 1 by the geometry route, already spends the fraction of the 6.0 us budget recorded above. Everything else on an item -- verb block, its inverse, the question effect -- must fit in what remains, AT THE SAME GEOMETRY, because the interaction is always on and the atoms do not move mid-sequence. That joint feasibility is exp71's first real question and this spike deliberately does not answer it.

Q5_pulser_reverification.what: the best route-2 solutions rebuilt as real Pulser Sequences on AnalogDevice and re-run through Pulser's own emulator TWICE: once with ideal square pulses quantised to the channel's 4 ns clock, and once with `with_modulation=True`, which applies the channel's 8 MHz modulation bandwidth to the waveform
Q5_pulser_reverification.reading: THIS IS THE SPIKE'S MOST CONSEQUENTIAL RESULT AND IT IS A WARNING. The searched solutions are near-unit fidelity in the continuous-time propagator and degrade once the pulse train is put on the device's real timebase. The two costs separate cleanly and the ORDER is the finding: the 4 ns CLOCK QUANTISATION dominates (worst case recorded above), while the channel's 8 MHz modulation bandwidth costs roughly an order of magnitude less. The damage tracks the shortest block in the solution -- a sub-300 ns segment driven at large detuning is where the worst case comes from -- so it is a property of the SEARCH's output, not an inherent hardware limit. The design consequence is not 'analog is infeasible': it is that exp71 must optimise ON THE DEVICE CLOCK, with a minimum-segment-length constraint, from the first iteration -- never a continuous-time idealisation re-checked afterwards. exp37/exp37b's free-V, square-pulse, decay-free model never had to face this, which is precisely why its F = 1 does not transfer.

limitations: 3 square pulse blocks only; smooth or EOM-shaped waveforms are not searched
unitary, decay-free: no spontaneous emission, no laser noise, no atom loss, no shot noise, no finite-sampling error -- Pulser's NoiseModel exists and is deliberately NOT used here
Nelder-Mead from 16 seeds; a reported fidelity is a LOWER bound on the family's reachability, never a proof of unreachability (except Q2a, which is a symmetry proof and does not depend on the search)

3 noun pairs out of 24 nouns, and their frozen angles happen to cluster in |theta|, which inflates the route-1 symmetric ceiling; a sweep would report a lower ceiling and the doc must not quote route 1 as if it were general
no verb block, no question effect and no trained parameter is compiled here
route 2 traces out a spectator atom; residual data-spectator entanglement is absorbed into the mixed-state fidelity rather than charged separately
